speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To understand the extent of your nerve involvement, on a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate the severity of your pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient has a year-long history of burning neck and arm pain with paresthesias, progressing to bilateral hand weakness over the last three months, alongside a history of diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia. Given these symptoms, have you noticed any numbness in your inner arms or hands that changes position when you turn your head?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). The combination of upper motor neuron signs (burning pain, paresthesias) and distinct lower motor neuron signs (absent reflexes, fasciculations, weakness) in a patient with a year-long progressive history is highly characteristic of ALS.
